CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFSELECT

CFSELECT writes an HTML SELECT control inside a CFFORM. It can build its OPTION list from a query, pre-select one or more values, and require the user to choose something.

Category

Forms

Syntax

<CFSELECT NAME="name"
    SIZE="integer"
    MULTIPLE="Yes/No"
    REQUIRED="Yes/No"
    MESSAGE="text"
    ONERROR="javascript_function"
    QUERY="query_name"
    VALUE="column_name"
    DISPLAY="column_name"
    SELECTED="value_list"
    PASSTHROUGH="HTML_attributes">
  optional OPTION tags
</CFSELECT>

Attributes

NAME
Required. Name of the form field.
SIZE
Optional. Number of visible rows; 1 (the default) gives a drop-down list.
MULTIPLE
Optional, default "No". Yes lets the user pick several entries; the field then arrives as a comma-separated list.
REQUIRED
Optional, default "No". Yes: the user must pick an entry whose value is not empty.
MESSAGE
Optional. Alert text when REQUIRED fails. Default "Error in fieldname."
ONERROR
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion always uses the standard alert.
QUERY
Optional. Query whose rows become OPTION tags.
VALUE
Required with QUERY. Column that supplies each option's value.
DISPLAY
Optional. Column that supplies the visible text. Defaults to the VALUE column.
SELECTED
Optional. Value, or comma-separated list of values, of the query options to pre-select.
PASSTHROUGH
Optional. Extra HTML attributes copied into the SELECT tag as they are.

Usage

OPTION tags you write between the start and end tags are kept and appear after the options built from the query. SELECTED applies to the query options only; for your own options write SELECTED in the OPTION tag as usual.

With CFFORM PRESERVEDATA="Yes", the submitted value overrides SELECTED, so the list remembers the user's choice.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFPARAM NAME="Form.Dept" DEFAULT="3">
<CFPARAM NAME="Form.Perks" DEFAULT="">

<CFQUERY NAME="GetDepts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT Dept_ID, Dept_Name FROM Departments ORDER BY Dept_Name
</CFQUERY>

<CFIF IsDefined("Form.FieldNames")>
  <CFOUTPUT><P>You picked department #Form.Dept# and the perks: #Form.Perks#</CFOUTPUT>
</CFIF>

<CFFORM NAME="Transfer" ACTION="cfselect.cfm">
<P>Department:
<CFSELECT NAME="Dept" QUERY="GetDepts" VALUE="Dept_ID"
    DISPLAY="Dept_Name" SELECTED="#Form.Dept#">
</CFSELECT>
<P>Perks (pick at least one):<BR>
<CFSELECT NAME="Perks" SIZE="4" MULTIPLE="Yes" REQUIRED="Yes"
    MESSAGE="Choose at least one perk.">
  <OPTION>Free coffee
  <OPTION>Parking space
  <OPTION>Y2K bonus
  <OPTION>Window office
</CFSELECT>
<P><INPUT TYPE="Submit" VALUE="Submit">
</CFFORM>
